University of Alberta, Envision Energy Reduction Master Plan 2022–30 (Nov 2021; J.B. upload 16 Oct 2026): targets for 2030 — energy intensity 15% below 2019/20, 350,000 GJe total reduction and 25,000 t CO2e from 2022, 2,500 kW renewable and 495 kW alternative energy installed; integrates with the Master Energy Plan for the District Energy System serving the Greater Campus Area; building measures include waste heat recovery (air and water) and micro-steam CHP turbines; laboratories use about 2.5× the energy of office or classroom space; programme of $3.56 M, 375,600 GJe, 30,450 t CO2e (savings valued at 2020/21 utility costs)

Alberta Agriculture and Irrigation (E. A. Laate), Economics of production and marketing greenhouse crops in Alberta 2023 (J.B. upload 16 Oct 2026): 53 growers, 909,443 m² surveyed; Alberta greenhouse area about 2.30 million m²; average investment $105.06 (lettuce) to $478.16 (tree seedlings) per m²; natural gas cost $3.99–12.47 per m² by crop (Table 23); about 85% of growers heat with natural gas, 9% propane (2019–20); forced-air furnaces most common, 30% hot-water and steam boilers; Alberta gas averaged $4.30/GJ (net farm, Jan 2021–Dec 2023) — https://open.alberta.ca

BC Jobs Plan, Special Report on the Greenhouse Sector (BC Ministries of Agriculture, Energy and others, report dated 24 Jan 2012; J.B. upload 16 Oct 2026): energy about 15% of operating costs (Statistics Canada 2011); most heat from natural gas, over half of production area also uses wood biomass; from May to October 90% of greenhouse natural gas is used to produce CO2, not heat, about 50% of annual gas; vegetable greenhouses 13,000–20,000 GJ/ha/yr (industry estimate, down from 22,500–28,000 in 2005); BC carbon tax a cost pressure.
